 JUDGMENT
This petition Under section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of .15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. It is stated that on 25.07.2020 at about 11.20 am., when the petitioner was a pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing No.KA-08-R-7924 ridden by her father i.e., 2 nd respondent herein.

When he reached near ITC Factory, on Malur Taluk, Kolar District, at that time another motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845 took a right turn to go to Goshala without observing the ongoing movements of the vehicle on the main road without putting indicator light and also without showing hand signals.
Due to which the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845 could not able to anticipate the negligent act of the 2 nd respondent, dashed against the 2nd respondent's motor cycle.
Due to impact, petitioner knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the petitioner was shifted Bharani Hospital, Malur, wherein she took first aid treatment.

Thereafter,
she was referred to Brindhavan Areion Hospital, Chamarajpet, Bangalore, wherein it was diagnosed as RTA with genital injury with primary ASARP, wherein she underwent perineal tear repair,
vaginoplasty, ano redoplasty, perineal body construction, levator complex repair.
She took treatment from 25.07.2020 to 31.07.2020 and till today she is taking treatment as outpatient.
The treated doctor has clearly opined that the prospects of marriage may not be possible due to severe perineal injury involving vagina and canal deep inside about some inches.

3. It is further submitted that, prior to accident petitioner was a student studying in convent at Malur and in future she cannot play any games like her friends due to disability and impediments and the petitioner is physically and functionally disabled.
The petitioner's mother has spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards treatment, medicine, conveyance etc., and she may require more amount for her future treatment.
The jurisdictional police have conducted investigation and charge sheet was filed against the riders of the both the motor cycle under Section 279, 337 & 338 of IPC.

As the accident was caused due to negligence of the both the riders of the vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 & 2 being RC owner of the motor cycle and 3rd respondent being insurer of the Honda Activa Motor cycle, bearing Regn.No.KA-08-R-7924 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation 4.
In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 to 3 have appeared before the Court through their counsel.
Respondent No.1 & 3 have filed their written statement.
Respondent No.2 did not file written statement.
Hence written statement of respondent No.2 is taken as Nil.

2 5. Respondent No.1 has filed its objection denying the petition averments.
He has admitted that he is the RC owner of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-08-R-7924.

The injured minor petitioner namely Sannidi.S was going towards ITC Factory, Malur-Hosakote Road, Malur Town, Kolar District as pillion rider by seat facing towards opposite direction without any hold on the motor cycle.

On the way at about 11.20 a.m., near ITC Factory, on Malur-Hosakote Road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District the rider G.V.Prakash over took the 1st respondent's motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05- EH-2845 and taken a right turn to go to Goshala without observing the movements of the ongoing vehicles on the Main Road without putting indicator light and showing any hand signals.

The alleged accident took place only due to the negligence of G.V.Prakash the rider of complainant motor cycle and not due to the negligence on the part of 1 st respondent's motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845 by its rider.
He has denied the injuries sustained, expenses incurred towards treatment of minor petitioner.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
Hence prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. Respondent No.3 - Insurance Company filed its objection denying the petition averments.
This respondent has contended that this Court has not territorial jurisdiction to entertain the claim petition.
Moreover, there is no declaration to the effect that no other claim petition is filed before any other Forum/Tribunal on the same cause of action.

It has contended that the Tribunal, even otherwise, is under statutory obligation under Rule 235 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 to send notices to owner/s and drivers of the vehicles said to have been involved in an accident and call upon them to produce any evidence they may wish to tender on issue of negligence and as held by Apex Court in case of Machindranath Kernath Kasar V/s D.S.Mylarappa & Ors on 29th April, 2008,
[2008 ACJ Pg 1964] wherein it is held that " Driver is a necessary party to decide issue of negligence".

entities.text: Machindranath Kernath Kasar V/s D.S.Mylarappa & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Principles of natural justice demand that person/s must be given an opportunity to defend his/their action before held responsible or liable for his/their alleged action, omission or commission.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has admitted the issuance of policy in favour of 3rd respondent in respect of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845, the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It has contended that the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-R-7924 was not holding valid DL at the time of accident and it had no valid and effective driving licence to drive class/type of vehicle allegedly involved in the alleged accident and thereby there was breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

Further it has denied the manner of accident, treatment taken by the minor petitioner,
injuries sustained and expenses incurred towards treatment, medicine conveyance etc.
7.

Further this respondent has also contended that the jurisdictional Police have investigated and filed a charge sheet against the Owner and rider of the Motor Cycle, bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845 for the alleged offence punishable U/Sec.196, 187 of MV Act, 1988 and 338, 279 of IPC 1860, however on learning that the offending vehicle was not insured the claimant has come with changed version of the alleged accident to claim compensation from this respondent attributing negligence on her father as well as who is the 2nd respondent herein which is in complete departure from the complaint.

Without prejudice to the stand taken above, alternatively this respondent that petitioner being daughter of the insured and represented by mother would steps into the shoes of the Owner and cannot be construed as third party.

The compensation claimed Sannidhi.S vs Harish B.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104032568/
3 is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed:-

ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 25.07.2020 at about 11.20 a.m., minor petitioner was going near ITC Factory, on Malur-Hosakote Road, Malur Taluk, Kolar District as a pillion rider in a Honda Activa Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08- R-7924 ridden by her father/2nd respondent without observing the movements of the ongoing vehicles on the main road without putting indicator light, in the result the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845 dashed against the 2nd respondent's motor cycle, due to the impact she knocked down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body mentioned in the petition?
2.
Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so, from which respondent?
3.

or Award?

The respondent No.1 has examined the rider of the motorcycle by name Sathish.B.N as RW-2 and got marked the two documents as Ex.R-3 to 4 and respondents evidence is taken as closed.

ACJ 2015 ACJ 1441 (Khenyei V/s New India Assurance Co., Ltd., & Ors.)

Issue No.1: In the Partly Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 12. ISSUE No.1:- In order to prove her claim, the mother of minor petitioner is examined as PW.1 has relied on the police and medical records.
She has deposed that on on 25.07.2020 at about 11.20 pm., when the petitioner was a pillion rider on the motor cycle bearing No.KA-08-R-7924 ridden by her father i.e., 2 nd respondent herein.

When he reached near ITC Factory, on Malur Taluk, Kolar Sannidhi.S vs Harish B.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104032568/

Due to which the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845 could not able to anticipate the negligent act of the 2nd respondent, dashed against the 2nd respondent's motor cycle.
Due to impact, petitioner knocked down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted Bharani Hospital,
Malur, wherein she took first aid treatment.

Thereafter, she was referred to Brindhavan Areion Hospital, Chamarajpet, Bangalore, wherein it was diagnosed as RTA with genital injury with primary ASARP, wherein she underwent perineal tear repair, vaginoplasty, ano redoplasty, perineal body construction, levator complex repair.

13. In support of her claim she has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P1, copy of complaint at Ex.P2, copy of spot mahazar at Ex.P3, copy of seizure mahazar at Ex.P4, copy of notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act at Ex.P5, copy of reply to notice U/Sec.133 of MV Act at Ex.P6, copy of IMV Report at Ex.P7, copy of wound certificate at Ex.P8, copy of charge sheet at Ex.P9, copy of Discharge summary at Ex.P10 and Ex.P11 copy of OPD records.

Perused the charge sheet Ex.P-8 against the rider and owner of the motorcycle KA-05 EH- 2845 for the offence punishable U/s.279, 337 & 308 of IPC and U/s.196 of M.V.Act.
14.

Learned counsel for petitioner vehemently argued that as per first information report the accident occurred only due to negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle KA-05 EH-2845 as such the respondent No.1 only liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

The petitioners while filing the claim petition they have alleged that the accident occurred due to negligence of rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845 and rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-R- 7924.
PW.1 in her examination she has deposed that due to negligence of rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845 and rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-R-7924 accident occurred.

In her cross-examination she has deposed that " 
    .     
  .
Further deposed that            ."
On perusal of documents placed by the petitioners it clearly shows that accident occurred only due to negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle.
The petitioner except examined PW.1 he has not proved the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No. KA-08-R-7924.

Even there is no evidence before the tribunal to show the rider and owner of the motorcycle KA-05 EH-2845 challenged the charge sheet filed by the I.O.
Sannidhi.S vs Harish B.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104032568/
5 15.

Learned counsel for the petitioner by relying upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in 2015 ACJ 1441 in Khenyei V/s New India Assurance company Limited and others vehemently argued that it is a contributory negligence,the petitioners can claim compensation on either of the parties.

entities.text: Khenyei V/s New India Assurance company Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hon'ble Apex Court in the above reported judgment held that:
"There is a difference between contributory and composite negligence.

In the case of contributory negligence, a person who has himself contributed to the accident cannot claim compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the accident to the extent of his own negligence.
Extent of his negligence is required to be determined as damages recoverable by him in respect of the injuries have to be reduced in proportion to his contributory negligence.
However, in the case of composite negligence, a person who has suffered has not contributed to the accident but due to the outcome of combination of negligence of two or more other persons.
In such case, the plaintiff/claimant is entitled to sue both or any one of the joint tortfeasors and to recover the entire compensation as liability of joint tortfeasors is joint and several."

16. This tribunal already held that the accident occurred only due to negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle and there is no negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08 R-7924.
This tribunal only fixed negligence on the rider of the motorcycle.
So, under such circumstances the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in above reported judgment is not helpful to the case of petitioner.
17. On meticulous perusal of the entire case, there is no evidence before the tribunal to show that the accident occurred due to negligence of rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08-R-7924.
Even on perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, the respondent No.3 elicited from her mouth to prove the negligence of rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845.
So, all the oral and documentary evidence placed by the petitioner, it is crystal clear that minor petitioner as a pillion rider on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-08R-7924.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral and documentary evidence of both parties, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the motorcycle KA-05 EH-2845 and petitioner is sustained to injuries.
Hence, Issue No.1 answered partly in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2:-
In view of discussion made while answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the minor petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount of Rs.2,00,000/- spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, disability, loss of amenities etc.
19.
It is relevant to note that the age of minor petitioner is shown as 6 years as on the date of accident.
In this regard PW-1 has produced Ex.P.13
the copy of Aadhar card of petitioner
. As per this document the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 06.05.2014 and the accident took place on 25.07.2020.
Therefore, it is clear that as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 6 years.

At this juncture, it is relevant to refer the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2445 between Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Company Ltd and another, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held as follows:
If the disability is upto 10% to the whole body R s . 1 lakh, above 10% and upto 30%
to the whole body, Rs. 3 lakhs: upto 60%, Rs. 4 lakhs, Upto 90% Rs.5 lakhs and above 90% it should be Rs. 6 lakhs.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
For all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc.,
21. In the instant case the petitioner has not examined doctor to prove the degree of her disability.
As already stated supra, absolutely there is nothing on record to show the extent of disability of petitioner caused due to accident.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to that effect, this Tribunal is not inclined to accept the version of the petitioner that she is having permanent disability caused in the accident.
22. The petitioner has not examined the doctor and there is no disability certificate.

As per guidelines issued by the Central Government for the purpose of assessing the extent of specified disability in a person included under the rights of persons with disability Act 2016 dated 04-01-2018, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not come under the any disability.

entities.text: rights of persons with disability Act 2016
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, the injuries sustained by the petitioner do not cause any disability for the petitioner's body or part of the body.
However, in view of the injury sustained by him in the accident he had suffered pain.
23. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Petitioner has sought for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in road traffic accident.
The petitioner has not produced any medicals bills and other bills to show the expenses incurred by her, only produced the wound certificate and discharge summary.
24. The natural guardian/mother of minor petitioner has contended that due to accident her daughter sustained grievous injuries.
In order to prove the injuries caused to her, she has produced Ex.P.8 wound certificate and Ex.P.10 discharge summary.

On perusal of Ex.P.8 it is clear that the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
1) Contusion injury over right frontal region 2) Perineal injury involving vagina, anal canal and deep inside about 4-4.5 inches with bleeding.
and also doctor opines that all the injuries are grievous in nature.

As per Ex.P.10 - discharge summary issued by Brindhavan Areion Hospital which discloses that, she took treatment from 25.07.2020 to 31.07.2020 i.e., for 6 days, which discloses that on examination it was found - Petitioner was admitted with history of RTA, on clinical examination and investigation were done.
MRI pelvis showed small sub centimeter sized cyst within left iliac bone in perarticular region.
Oedema/contusion of the soft tissues in the upper medial thigh and perineal region.

No evidence of Sannidhi.S vs Harish B.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104032568/
7 fracture.
Paediatric Surgeon opinion was taken and posted for the surgery.
After taken written consent child underwent Perineal tear repair + vaginoplasty + Ano redoplasty + Perineal body reconstruction + levator complex repair under General Anaesthesia on 26.07.2020.
But there are no evidences that the Petitioner is suffering from any difficulties which would affect her livelihood and day-today activities and earning capacity.
In the absence of medical evidence to prove disability, I deem it proper to award global compensation.

By considering the nature of injuries, age of the petitioner, treatment taken in the hospital as stated supra and considering the pain and sufferings by the Petitioner, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- as global compensation under all the conventional heads with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

25. Regarding Interest & Liability: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
The petitioner has filed petition against the respondent No.1 to 3.
This tribunal already held that the accident occurred only due to negligence on the part of rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-EH-2845.

On perusal of documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the respondent No.1 has not holding the insurance his motor cycle and police have filed charge sheet against the respondent No.2 for the offence punishable Under section 196 of MV Act.

Accordingly,
respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered partly in the Affirmative.

26. ISSUE NO.3: In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only)
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
The respondent No.1 Owner of the motorcycle bearing No. KA-05-EH-2845 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of this order.
The Petition against respondent No.2 and 3 is hereby dismissed.

After the deposit of compensation amount, since the petitioner is minor, the entire compensation amount shall be deposited in her name as fixed deposited in any nationalized bank/scheduled bank till she attains the age of majority.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral and documentary evidence of both parties, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of rider of the motorcycle KA-05 EH-2845 and petitioner is sustained to injuries.
To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount of Rs.2,00,000/- spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, disability, loss of amenities etc.
19.
Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to that effect, this Tribunal is not inclined to accept the version of the petitioner that she is having permanent disability caused in the accident.
22. The petitioner has not examined the doctor and there is no disability certificate.
As per guidelines issued by the Central Government for the purpose of assessing the extent of specified disability in a person included under the rights of persons with disability Act 2016 dated 04-01-2018, the injuries sustained by the petitioner are not come under the any disability.
Therefore, the injuries sustained by the petitioner do not cause any disability for the petitioner's body or part of the body.
However, in view of the injury sustained by him in the accident he had suffered pain.
In the absence of medical evidence to prove disability, I deem it proper to award global compensation.
By considering the nature of injuries, age of the petitioner, treatment taken in the hospital as stated supra and considering the pain and sufferings by the Petitioner, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- as global compensation under all the conventional heads with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
On perusal of documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the respondent No.1 has not holding the insurance his motor cycle and police have filed charge sheet against the respondent No.2 for the offence punishable Under section 196 of MV Act.
